slides.heading: Node Depths
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Easy · Binary Trees
slides.narration: Let's solve Node Depths, an easy binary trees problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Sum of the depths (distance from root) of every node.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Sum of the depths (distance from root) of every node.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Each node contributes its depth, so pass the depth down while traversing and add it up.
slides.narration: Each node contributes its depth, so pass the depth down while traversing and add it up.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Naive: compute each node's depth by walking up from it → O(n·h)
Optimal: pass depth down in one traversal → O(n)
BFS by levels also works: depth × level size
slides.narration: A naive approach finds each node's depth separately. Passing the depth down during one traversal gives linear time. A breadth-first version multiplies each level's size by its depth.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Traverse from the root at depth zero
2. Add the current depth to the total
3. Visit children with depth plus one
slides.narration: Step by step. First, traverse from the root at depth zero. Second, add the current depth to the total. Third, visit children with depth plus one. Fourth, return the sum.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of h.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Remember the root has depth zero, and an empty tree sums to zero.
